basis: Compared the two user-supplied City Council minutes with existing meeting pages and archived agenda inventories. Minutes establish the recorded motions; expenditure, implementation and contract terms remain separate. The September 15 G.16 vote result is absent from the supplied minutes and remains attributed to the previously reviewed transcript.

2026-09-15.label: September 15, 2026

items.title: Closed-session report
items.summary: The minutes report no reportable action on the City Manager evaluation or property negotiations.
items.limit: No reportable action is distinct from a public approval or a finding about confidential discussion.

items.title: Consent calendar approved; G.10 tabled
items.summary: Fenn moved and Martinez seconded approval of G.1–G.9 and G.11–G.15. G.10 was tabled, and G.16 was pulled for separate discussion. The minutes record unanimous approval of the grouped items.
items.limit: The G.1 minutes-date discrepancy is identified below. Report receipt and authorizations are not an audit of payments.

items.title: E-bike adoption motion recorded
items.summary: White moved and Lara seconded the motion to waive the full second reading and adopt the e-conveyance ordinance. The supplied minutes do not state the result or a vote total.
items.limit: The previously reviewed transcript supports the existing adoption and 5–0 account. Those details are transcript-based, not independently confirmed by this minutes file.

items.title: Cluck and Moo loan approved
items.summary: Council approved a $25,000 forgivable loan for application ED2026-0005, with a public-purpose finding. Voigt moved and Lara seconded.
items.limit: Loan forgiveness, disbursement, operating milestones, and contract corrections require their own evidence.

items.title: Finance Director agreement authorized
items.summary: Council authorized the City Manager to execute the Finance Director employment agreement for Travis Hickey. White moved and Voigt seconded.
items.limit: Salary and benefit figures in the earlier briefing are from the agreement and staff report; the minutes do not restate those figures.

items.title: Deputy City Manager agreement authorized
items.summary: Council authorized execution of Kari Mendoza’s Deputy City Manager employment agreement. Mendoza recused. Voigt moved and White seconded.
items.limit: Salary and benefit figures in the earlier briefing are from the agreement and staff report; the minutes do not restate those figures.

items.title: Oak Valley Parkway traffic-signal award approved
items.summary: Council awarded Calpromax Engineering the Oak Valley Parkway/Palm Avenue signal work for $847,090 plus $84,710 contingency, totaling $931,800. Voigt moved and White seconded.
items.limit: Authorization does not establish payment, completed work, or later implementation.

items.title: Xenia Avenue housing agreement approved
items.summary: Council approved the density bonus housing agreement with Xenia Avenue Housing Associates LP and authorized execution. The described project has 66 rental units, including 16 supportive-housing units. White moved and Martinez seconded.
items.limit: Agreement approval is not evidence that construction is complete or units are occupied.

items.title: Committee implementation documents directed
items.summary: Council directed staff to proceed with restructuring as adjusted and return with updated bylaws, resolutions and other implementing documents. Voigt moved and White seconded.
items.limit: This direction did not itself adopt every implementing ordinance. The October 20 first readings remain separately recorded.

items.title: Legislative update received
items.summary: Council received and filed the September legislative update. Voigt moved and Lara seconded.
items.limit: Receipt of an update does not adopt every policy or measure discussed.

2026-09-15.attendance: All five members were present. Regular session was called to order at 6:08 PM.

discrepancies.text: The supplied minutes say G.1 approved August 18 minutes, while the archived September 15 agenda attachment is labeled September 1 minutes. The date discrepancy is unresolved; neither source has been silently relabeled.

The supplied minutes record the motion to adopt the e-bike ordinance, with White moving and Lara seconding, but omit an explicit approval statement or vote total. The existing adoption and 5–0 account comes from the previously reviewed transcript, not this minutes file.

2026-10-06.label: October 6, 2026

items.title: Closed-session actions reported
items.summary: Council approved defense of the Ortega case on Lara’s motion, seconded by Voigt, and defense of the City and officer in the Hosie case on Voigt’s motion, seconded by Fenn. Each passed 4–0, Martinez absent. B.3–B.5 had no reportable action.
items.limit: The defense authorizations do not establish findings on the merits, liability, settlement, or case outcomes.

items.title: Consent calendar approved together
items.summary: Fenn moved and White seconded approval of the consent calendar. The minutes record 4–0 approval with Martinez absent. Items include September 15 minutes, warrants, wastewater and drainage actions, transit fares, holiday decorations, accounting support, speed limits and financial reports.
items.limit: Grouped approval does not independently verify individual payments or financial-report balances.

items.title: Holiday-decoration and accounting contract capacity increased
items.summary: Within the consent vote, Council increased Dekra-Lite’s aggregate ceiling from $260,000 to $500,000 within the approved budget, with up to 5% amendment/change-order authority. The LSL accounting agreement increased by $100,000 from $65,000 to $165,000.
items.limit: The Dekra-Lite motion requests no additional appropriation. Contract ceilings are not proof of expenditure.

items.title: Short-term rental hearing continued
items.summary: White moved and Voigt seconded continuation of the short-term-rental hearing and associated fees to October 20.
items.limit: This was a continuance, not adoption of the ordinance or fees. October 20 first-reading and fee actions remain separate.

items.title: Legislative recap received by consensus
items.summary: Council reached consensus to receive and file the California Public Policy Group legislative-session recap.
items.limit: Do not label this consensus as a separate 4–0 vote or legislative policy adoption.

items.title: Bicycle Classic and Beaumont Bicycle Day approved
items.summary: Council approved co-hosting Stage 2 of the 2027 Redlands Bicycle Classic on April 8, 2027, with youth bicycle races and a bicycle-themed Beaumont Nights event. The motion authorizes City operational resources and negotiation/execution of the MOU. White moved and Lara seconded.
items.limit: Route, schedule and operating details may be finalized within the approved authority. Approval is not proof that the future event has occurred.

items.title: Highland Springs smart-signal construction awarded
items.summary: Council awarded California Professional Engineering the signal smart-technology work for $723,517 plus $72,352 contingency, totaling $795,869. Voigt moved and Lara seconded.
items.limit: Authorization does not establish payment, completed work, or later implementation.

items.title: Playground and field-lighting equipment purchases approved
items.summary: Council approved $972,933.56 in combined equipment purchases for Sports Park and Wildflower Park, with maximum combined purchase authority of $1,021,580.23. The final motion uses remaining CIP P-04 savings for the playground purchase and contingency instead of CIP P25-05. Lara moved and Voigt seconded.
items.limit: Equipment purchasing authority is distinct from installation/construction costs and actual expenditure.

items.title: Temporary Trevino skate amenities authorized for competitive bidding
items.summary: Council authorized competitive bidding, agreements and a purchase order up to $120,000. Funding is $72,609.98 in savings ($67,462.16 from P-09 and $5,147.82 from P-20) plus $47,390.02 from P27-01. The motion requires staff to bring back a budget adjustment reallocating the funding source. Voigt moved and White seconded.
items.limit: This is procurement authority, not a direct award to American Ramp or proof that a contract, installation, or funding-source adjustment has been completed.

2026-10-06.attendance: Voigt, White, Fenn and Lara were present; Martinez was absent. Regular session was called to order at 6:07 PM.

discrepancies.text: The website previously retained an outcome-review-in-progress status. The supplied minutes now establish the recorded decisions and attendance; all recorded roll-call approvals were 4–0 with Martinez absent.
The legislative recap was received by consensus. It must not be described as a separate 4–0 roll-call vote.

The final motion specifies competitive bidding and execution authority up to $120,000, identifies the project-savings and Trevino Park funding split, and requires a later funding-source budget adjustment. This is not an award to the vendor whose proposal was attached to the agenda.
